response.title: How much battery do I need to run a well pump a few times a day for showers and flushing during a week-long outage?
response.answer:
For running a well pump a few times a day for showers and toilet flushing during a 7-day power outage, I'd start by looking at a 5 kWh LiFePO₄ battery system, with a sufficiently powerful inverter.

Depending on your pump and water usage, you might get away with 2–3 kWh, or need 10 kWh or more.

The biggest challenge is often starting the well pump, not supplying enough battery energy.

Estimated battery requirements

Assuming a typical 240V residential submersible well pump, a household of 2–4 people, and no battery recharging:

These are planning estimates assuming roughly 30–60 minutes of total pump operation per day, with battery and inverter losses and some reserve included. Actual runtime depends heavily on well depth, pumping rate, pressure settings, and water consumption.

What the setup might look like
Shop

5 kWh LiFePO₄ battery

A reasonable starting point for modest water use during a week-long outage.

Shop

120/240V split-phase pure sine wave inverter

Often around 4–6 kW continuous for a typical pump, but the motor's starting surge may require substantially more or a compatible soft starter.

Shop

Existing pressure tank

Stores pressurized water between pump cycles, so the pump doesn't need to run every time you flush.

A properly rated transfer switch or other approved isolation arrangement is also needed to connect the backup system safely. A 240V pump generally cannot run from an ordinary 120V portable power station outlet.

How much energy does pumping actually take?

For example, suppose your 1 HP pump draws 1,500 watts while operating and runs for 30 minutes each day.

Depending on your pump and water usage, you might get away with 2–3 kWh, or need 10 kWh or more.

## Estimated battery requirements

Assuming a typical 240V residential submersible well pump, a household of 2–4 people, and no battery recharging:

| Pump size | Estimated daily use | Battery for 7 days |
|---|---:|---:|
| ½ HP | 0.3–0.6 kWh | 3–5 kWh |
| ¾ HP | 0.4–0.8 kWh | 4–7 kWh |
| 1 HP | 0.5–1.0 kWh | 5–9 kWh |
| 1.5 HP | 0.7–1.5 kWh | 7–13 kWh |

        <radio value="240">240V</radio>

      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Number of people using water</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={people} onChange={setPeople}>
        <radio value="1">1</radio>
        <radio value="2">2</radio>
        <radio value="3">3</radio>
        <radio value="4">4</radio>
        <radio value="5+">5+</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Will you recharge the battery during the outage?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={recharge} onChange={setRecharge}>
        <radio value="none">No — battery only for 7 days</radio>
        <radio value="solar">Yes — solar panels</radio>
        <radio value="generator">Yes — generator</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate my battery size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
